avalancheActivity.highlights: Wind slabs along the border between Valais and France.
avalancheActivity.comment:
On wind-loaded slopes and on extremely steep slopes dry avalanches are possible, even medium-sized ones. Above approximately 2300 m they can be triggered in the new snow and wind slab layers and reach large size in some cases. As the day progresses the likelihood of loose snow slides being released will increase in particular on rocky slopes. Individual gliding avalanches can also occur, in particular on steep grassy slopes.

New snow and wind slabs can in some cases be released by a single winter sport participant. This applies in particular on very steep slopes. They represent the main danger. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher.

snowpackStructure.comment:
In particular in the northwest 15 to 30 cm of snow fell on Wednesday above approximately 1200 m. Little snow will fall until Thursday in some localities.

As a consequence of the occasionally strong northerly wind, fresh snow drift accumulations will form on Thursday.
Above approximately 2200 m there are 70 to 140 cm of snow, and even as much as 190 cm in some localities, especially above approximately 2500 m.
The snowpack is not distinctly layered. The snowpack will be unstable in some places. Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2500 m.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

tendency.highlights: The weather conditions will facilitate a gradual strengthening of the snowpack. The danger will decrease gradually.

region.name: B - VALLI DI GRESSONEY, AYAS, CHAMPORCHER

avalancheActivity.highlights: Little snow will fall until Thursday.
avalancheActivity.comment:
As a consequence of new snow and wind individual natural avalanches are possible as the day progresses. Mostly these are small. Above approximately 2300 m they can be released in the new snow and wind slab layers.

The wind slabs of the last few days can be released by a single winter sport participant in isolated cases.
Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher.

snowpackStructure.comment:
Over a wide area 15 to 20 cm of snow fell on Wednesday above approximately 1200 m. Little snow will fall until Thursday in some localities.
As a consequence of the strong northerly wind, fresh snow drift accumulations will form on Thursday.
Above approximately 2000 m there are 30 to 70 cm of snow, and even more in some localities.
The snowpack will be in some cases unstable.
Towards its base, the snowpack is moist, in particular below approximately 2500 m.
At low and intermediate altitudes only a little snow is lying.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field.

tendency.highlights: The weather conditions will foster a gradual strengthening of the near-surface layers. The danger will persist.
